Alex.note: Finley's Sphinx claim is a cat claim, and three others are already voting Finley. I'll throw my lowest card to add a vote.

Blair.note: Finley claimed Sphinx, a cat, so I'm confident Finley is Meowfia. Throwing my H10 at Finley banks 10 if Farm wins.

Casey.note: Finley is the vote target. I'll throw my Wild W5, a single vote that banks at 0 and costs me little if Farm wins.

Drew.note: Four Farm players are already voting Finley, so Finley is likely to be eggsecuted and my side can't stop it. I'll throw my wild W4 at Casey, a Farm player; if we lose, a thrown card on the other team returns to my nest.

Ellis.note: Voting Finley with two cards: the Wild and the 7, keeping my 9s and 13.

Finley.note: The table is set on me, so I'll throw at Casey, the most aggressive Farm voice. Casey is on the other team, so my highest thrown card returns if we lose; I'll throw only H3.

Alex.confusing:
The rule that Meowfia are at most 2 but the Farm throw-count was hard to track, and Casey's Pigeon claim was easy to misread as a lie when it was a Mouser visit. Also unclear: whether a Hawk egg confirms the target was Meowfia when the Hawk gains only if the target is Meowfia.</confusing>
<fun>Round 2, when Drew's Hawk egg lined up with my Owl read on Blair and the table converged on Blair in one vote.</fun>
<change>Make the dawn reports include visitor roles (not only counts) so that claims like Casey's Pigeon visit can be checked without guessing.</change>
<regret>In round 1 I threw at Casey on a count mismatch and nobody checked Casey's real role; I would have held my high cards longer and thrown only low ones until the Meowfia were confirmed. In round 3 I threw at Finley with Casey's Pigeon-style thin evidence, so I'd have asked Finley for a visit before calling the vote.</regret>

Blair.confusing: The dawn egg counts were hard to trace, since several roles (Pigeon, Owl, Eagle, Falcon) produced eggs that were easy to misattribute, and I couldn't tell which visit caused which change.
Blair.fun: Finley's last-beat Sphinx claim was a fun reveal: a Meowfia cat admitting its role to make the table reconcile its story, and the table turned on it fast.
Blair.change: I'd make Wink use more visible, since a player dying with no clue about who winked made the Round 2 vote hard to read.
Blair.regret: In Round 2 I winked Drew, who was a truthful Farm Hawk and the only player whose story backed up my own visit; I should have kept the Wink and argued my own egg count instead.

Casey.confusing: The egg-count mechanics were hard to track, especially how visits, Owl and Eagle reports, and Falcon and Hawk eggs interact. I also wasn't sure whether a dead player's throw still counts for the cards banked.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when the Hawk's egg exposed Blair as the target and the table turned on them in one day, was a satisfying read.
Casey.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since many claims were hard to verify from egg counts alone.
Casey.regret: In round 1 as Mouser I winked Drew, a Farm player, instead of protecting my own cover. I should have backed a consistent Pigeon story or thrown at Alex to shift the vote.

Drew.confusing: The Sphinx was hard to read: Finley's claim was true, but as a Meowfia it looked like a lie to the Farm players, and I couldn't tell which Meowfia was which. Egg-count reconciliation also took a lot of attention.
Drew.fun: Round 1 was satisfying: Alex's Eagle count and Casey's Pigeon claim mismatched, and the table caught Casey through the nest sizes. Casey's Pigeon story unraveled on the day's own egg counts.
Drew.change: I would make the Storyteller state which Meowfia are still alive, or at least a Meowfia's teammates, so that a Meowfia player doesn't have to guess who their partner is.
Drew.regret: As Meowfia in round 3 I hugged Ellis and stayed mostly silent, then threw at Casey, a Farm player, while Finley, my teammate, was voted out. I would have kept my visit claim quieter and used my throw to protect the side rather than hit a Farm player.

Ellis.confusing: The Falcon's dawn report was hard to read: no egg meant the target visited someone, and I briefly misjudged which result cleared or implicated a player. Tracking how night outcomes depended on other players' actions took effort.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when Alex's Owl read and my Falcon visit both pointed at Blair, and Drew's Hawk egg confirmed it. The table cross-checked egg counts well.
Ellis.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so players can verify claims without guessing at the egg rules.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I accepted Drew's visit story without pressing harder, though Drew was the Floofer and hugging/visit claims were worth testing earlier.

Finley.confusing: The Wink-style collapses were confusing: Drew died twice with no visible cause, and nobody could tell who had winked. Tracking the Owl and Falcon egg counts against each other was also hard to follow.
Finley.fun: Round 1's egg-count debate, where Casey's Pigeon claim got cross-checked against Alex's nest and the table converged on a vote. It felt like real detective work.
Finley.change: Publish which animal or action caused each death or collapse, so the table can check claims against real events.
Finley.regret: In Round 2 I helped push the vote onto Blair, my Meowfia teammate, and kept quiet while the table converged on them. Instead I should have deflected suspicion toward a Farm player and kept Blair's position intact.

review.title: Wink, Then Wilt
review.headline: Meowfia lost every vote while Drew banked 22 points as a corpse.
review.summary: Farm won all three rounds. Each time the table agreed on a target by checking egg counts against claims, and Meowfia could not break the logic. Drew was winked twice in two rounds yet still threw big cards and won the game with 24. The Wink killed accusers but did not save either Mouser.

rounds.recap: Casey (Mouser) claimed Pigeon, but Alex's +1 came from his own Eagle visit and Finley's Owl saw only an Eagle visit Casey. Casey winked Drew, which backfired and the table piled on Casey. Drew still threw C9 from the grave and banked 9.

Drew's Hawk egg from visiting Blair exposed Blair, the Mouser. Blair winked Drew, but Alex's Owl and Ellis's Falcon both confirmed visits to Blair. Blair was eggsecuted. Drew, dead, banked a 7 and reached 22.
Finley (Sphinx) held back his role, then claimed Sphinx when pressed, which is a cat. Five throws went at him. Drew, the other Meowfia, stayed quiet and escaped. Farm won again.

highlights.text: Casey winks Drew mid-accusation. It looks like a clean silencing, but it only confirms Casey's guilt.
Drew's Hawk egg plus Alex's Owl report (Falcon, Hawk visited Blair) forms a tight evidence chain. Blair winks Drew, but it is too late.
Finley refuses to name his role. Alex presses, and he finally says Sphinx, a cat, and the table throws at him.
Drew, Meowfia, stays quiet and defends Finley only mildly. He survives and wins the game on 24.

confusions.what: Claimed a +1 egg came from a visitor. He then said it came from his own Eagle visit, but the Eagle gains an egg per visitor and Casey had one (Finley). He also first said Drew's visit explained it, though Drew is a Hawk and lays no egg on others.
Said Casey's Pigeon visit explained Alex's +1, then used the opposite fact to accuse Casey. His reasoning flipped within one round.
Claimed Pigeon, but a Pigeon's egg shows in the target's nest. The claim contradicted Alex's count, so the bluff could not work.
Said Ellis's Falcon visit giving no egg cleared Blair. A Falcon only gains an egg if the target visited no one, so it fits her story. Ellis corrected her.
Said Casey's Pigeon visit never happened because of an Owl report. The Owl only shows an Eagle visited Casey, so this does not prove the Pigeon claim false.
Treated Finley's Sphinx claim as proof he is Meowfia. The claim was true, but she called it a tell without any role-check.
Told the table he visited Ellis, though he had said he visited Casey and was an Owl in round 1. This was cross-round confusion in his own cover story.

worked: The egg-count cross-check carried the game. Drew's Hawk egg, Alex's Owl report and Ellis's Falcon visit locked together in round 2 to expose Blair.
The Wink gave Meowfia a real decision, and its anonymity made the dead player's silence a clue in itself.
Dead players still throwing cards and banking points created a sharp scoring twist: Drew was winked twice and still won.
problems: Meowfia lost all three votes and never came close. Hidden partners, one or two cats, and a Farm-heavy pool of checkable visit results make bluffing nearly impossible. Consider more Meowfia information or Farm roles that give weaker or noisier results.
The Wink backfires. It removes an accuser but the dead player keeps scoring, so it gave Drew the win. Either dead players' throws should score less, or the Wink should cost the winker something.

Final standings were set by round 1 and round 2 throws from a dead Drew, not by who played better. The score race gave nobody real tension, since every Farm player had the same incentive to vote the same target.

Claiming a Farm role as Meowfia is risky because other roles' reports disprove it. A fake Pigeon, Sphinx or silent claim lost every time. Meowfia need a safe cover role or less checkable Farm results.
The 'CAW CAW' rule and the four-beat day made players repeat the same points. Round 3 stalled for several turns with everyone saying counts reconcile. Shorten the day or reward new information.
